# SK9008 — The canonical block has been edited

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

The managed block between `# skala:canonical begin` and `# skala:canonical end` no longer hashes to the SHA-256 its own marker carries: somebody edited it in place. Move the edit below `# skala:local begin`, where it survives every canonical bump, then `skala config sync --apply` restores the block. Exit 3 from `skala config diff --canonical` and exit 1 from `skala config check`, both without `--strict`; `canonical.drift` in `skala.jsonc` lowers it to `warning` or `off`.

|---|---|

| Since | 0.6 |

## Why

Drift is the gate condition of canonical distribution (docs/plan/03 § "Canonical distribution"). The canonical must physically be the repository's `.editorconfig`, so the only thing that stops it silently becoming a local fork is a hash the tool checks. An edit inside the block is lost on the next bump; an edit below the local marker survives every bump, because later sections win — which is why the remedy moves the line rather than deleting it. The hash is over the LF-normalised payload with one trailing newline, so line-ending churn and a trailing blank line are not drift, and a comment added inside the block is.

## When it does not fire

The same id is also raised — at warning, and not subject to the policy — when `skala.jsonc` sets `canonical.drift` to something other than `error`, `warning` or `off`; the policy then falls back to `error`. A file with no markers at all is `SK9014`, not drift, and a retyped marker that does not match case-sensitively reads as unmanaged rather than drifted. Drift and `SK9009` are mutually exclusive: an edited block is never reported as merely behind.

## Configuration

- `skala.jsonc: canonical.drift`
